title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with funding rounds and strategic partnerships as companies vie for dominance in the evolving landscape. Meanwhile, the U.S. government is ramping up its budget for space resilience amidst increasing competition and infrastructure challenges.

themes.title: Funding Frenzy Continues
themes.body: Tomorrow.io's latest $35 million injection and True Anomaly's $190 million Series C highlight a robust appetite for investment in space tech. This influx of capital suggests investors are betting on the long-term viability of commercial space ventures.

themes.title: Military Focus on Space Operations
themes.body: The Pentagon's increased budget for space resilience and the collaboration between Anduril and L3Harris on a tactical SDA constellation signal a shift towards prioritizing military capabilities in orbit. As the next war is expected to be fought in space, these developments underscore the urgency of enhancing U.S. space operations.

themes.title: Satellite Launch Proliferation Ahead
themes.body: A new CSF report forecasts over 7,000 satellites launched annually by the mid-2030s, raising questions about the adequacy of U.S. launch infrastructure. This anticipated surge will likely strain existing capabilities and necessitate innovative solutions.

themes.title: Geopolitical Tensions in Space
themes.body: Increased Russian co-orbital activity near commercial GEO slots and GPS jamming incidents highlight the growing geopolitical stakes in space. As nations assert their presence, the implications for commercial operations and security are becoming increasingly complex.
